topic: the rooms nobody stages because nobody stages them
angle: NAR's own staging survey shows the living room staged 91% of the time and the bedroom 83%. Every other room is where a listing is actually lost, and those are the rooms a seller can stage themselves for free.
palette: sea glass green and chalk with pale brass
visualSummary: One bare bathroom source photograph across the top of the deep blue field, then the same bathroom staged below in an asymmetric grid alongside the other rooms sellers skip, each panel carrying a style pill and a one line note naming the room and how often it gets staged
whyNow: NAR's February 2025 staging survey puts the living room at 91%, the primary bedroom at 83% and the dining room at 69%, so the rest of the house is measurably unstaged. With 20.4% of August 2026 listings already cutting price and inventory up 3.6% year over year, the unstaged rooms are what a buyer compares.
whyThisEarnsAClick: The reader opens their own listing and counts. Every room they find unstaged is a free render they have a reason to run tonight.

topic: one kitchen photographed once and returned in three finishes
angle: A seller does not have to guess which look sells. The same kitchen photograph comes back in three presets and the market picks, not the seller's taste.
palette: caramel timber and cream with brushed steel
visualSummary: An empty pale kitchen across the top of the deep blue field, then the same kitchen rendered three ways in an asymmetric grid below, each panel with a style pill and a single line naming who it is for
whyNow: Realtor.com named 27 September to 3 October 2026 the best week of the year to buy, with active listings 13.3% above the average week. The buyer has more to choose from that week than any other, so the kitchen has to read to more than one of them.
whyThisEarnsAClick: The reader wants to know which preset their own kitchen suits, and only their own photo answers that.

topic: telling the room what is wrong with it in one sentence
angle: A seller already knows what their living room lacks. The AI Designer takes that sentence directly, so there is nothing to translate into a preset.
palette: caramel leather and oat wool over walnut
visualSummary: Full bleed living room split by a wipe, the empty room above the line and the same room staged below it, with the typed instruction set as the headline over a bottom scrim
whyNow: Daylight shortens through late September and showings move into the evening, so warmth is what an autumn listing photograph has to carry.
whyThisEarnsAClick: The reader has their own sentence ready and can only find out whether it works by typing it.

topic: how many seconds a listing photo gets before the scroll
angle: A checkable figure for how little time the first photograph has, set against how many listings are competing for it this month.
palette: warm white tile and honey oak
visualSummary: A very large brand blue numeral on the deep blue field with a white claim line under it and a photo band of a staged kitchen across the lower third
whyNow: A 2026 industry analysis measured 2.7 seconds on a listing's primary photo. In August 2026 inventory rose 3.6% year over year, so there are more photographs competing for those seconds.
whyThisEarnsAClick: The number is small enough to be alarming and checkable against their own listing's first image.

topic: a dorm room furnished from the floor plan before the lease starts
angle: A student signs for a room they have never stood in. The floor plan is the only thing they hold, and it can be rendered into a photograph.
palette: birch ply and slate blue with white
visualSummary: A flat line drawing of a small single room above the wipe and the photoreal rendered dorm below it

copy.headline: You signed for a floor plan.

whyNow: Term has started and the late lettings are the ones taken sight unseen.
whyThisEarnsAClick: A plan is the only asset this reader has, so they upload it to see. Risk: the before half is a drawing we would have to source or fabricate.

topic: whether a staged photo has to look expensive to work
angle: Sellers assume staging means luxury. The plainest preset tends to win because it reads as a house somebody lives in rather than a showroom.
palette: oatmeal linen and clay with black iron
visualSummary: One empty living room at the top, then the same room in standard, coastal and midcentury below, the plainest panel sitting largest in the grid
whyNow: The median list price fell 1.3% year over year in August 2026, the tenth straight month of declines, so buyers are pricing the house rather than admiring it.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It contradicts what the reader expected, so the only way to settle it is on their own room.

topic: the same room read by two different buyers
angle: A family and a downsizing couple want opposite things from one room. One photograph cannot say both, and it no longer has to.
palette: sand and washed indigo with rope
visualSummary: An empty living room across the top and two large staged versions below, each labelled with the buyer it is aimed at
whyNow: Autumn buyers are fewer and deadline driven, so they self select quickly and the photograph has to do the sorting.
whyThisEarnsAClick: The reader wants to know which of the two their own room already reads as.

topic: the price cut a seller takes instead of a better photograph
angle: One in five listings on the market in August cut its price. A price cut is expensive and a render is free, and most sellers try them in the wrong order.
palette: teak and mustard over cream
visualSummary: A very large brand blue percentage numeral on the deep blue field, a white claim line under it, a muted supporting sentence, and a band of a staged living room across the lower third
whyNow: 20.4% of active listings carried a price reduction in August 2026, and the median home sat 60 days. The seller reading this is inside that window right now.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It puts a number on the alternative the reader is already considering, and the cheaper option takes one upload.

topic: sending the staged photos to someone who has no account
angle: A seller wants a partner or an agent to look before anything goes live. A share link opens with no signup on the other end.
palette: teak and mustard over cream
visualSummary: A large short phrase on the deep blue field with a staged living room band beneath it
whyNow: Autumn sellers decide as a household against a year end deadline.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Weakly. It removes a small friction, and the proof needs a screenshot of the product rather than a room.

topic: the studio in the language the seller actually speaks
angle: Eleven languages. A seller does not have to work in English to stage their own house.
palette: terracotta and lime plaster with pale oak
visualSummary: A large numeral eleven on the deep blue field with a staged kitchen band under it
whyNow: Nothing seasonal, which is the weakness.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Weakly. It matters to a small slice of the audience and the proof is an interface screenshot.

topic: asking for the one thing the bathroom is missing
angle: Sellers know what is wrong with a room and cannot say it to a dropdown. A sentence is the interface.
palette: sea salt and driftwood with pale brass
visualSummary: A bare bathroom above the wipe and the same bathroom below after a typed instruction, the instruction itself carried as the headline over a bottom scrim

copy.headline: Add a plant and warmer light.

whyNow: Showings run into the evening from late September, so lighting is what the photograph has to fix.
whyThisEarnsAClick: The reader has a sentence of their own ready to test.

topic: a kitchen that does not exist yet, sold from the drawing
angle: A renovation is currently sold on a flat plan. The plan can be a photograph instead.
palette: caramel timber and cream with brushed steel
visualSummary: A flat kitchen plan above the wipe and the photoreal rendered kitchen below it

copy.headline: Sell the kitchen you have not built.

whyNow: Autumn is when renovation decisions get made for a spring start.
whyThisEarnsAClick: The reader has a plan drawing sitting in an email. Risk: the before half has to be a genuine plan, not a fabricated one.

topic: the three photographs a first time seller gets wrong
angle: Three specific errors, each visible in the reader's own camera roll right now.
palette: oatmeal linen and clay with black iron
visualSummary: A large numeral three on the deep blue field over a staged living room band
whyNow: September listings are going up now.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Checkable against their own phone, but a stat card cannot actually show three mistakes in one frame.

topic: a small bathroom that reads larger once it is furnished
angle: Bathrooms are the room sellers believe cannot be staged. They are the room where staging changes the perceived size most, because there is no furniture to hide behind.
palette: warm white tile and honey oak
visualSummary: A bare bathroom above the wipe and the same bathroom styled below it, same camera position
whyNow: With inventory up 3.6% year over year, an incomplete listing loses to a complete one on the same street.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It contradicts an assumption the reader holds, though the claim is softer than the NAR figure behind i01.

topic: one photograph of a spare room returned in seven finishes
angle: Seven presets exist. A seller does not have to choose one before seeing all of them.
palette: sand and washed indigo with rope
visualSummary: One empty room at the top and a dense grid of style pills below it
whyNow: Evergreen, which is the weakness.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Breadth is a reason to try rather than a reason to click, and seven panels at feed size are seven thumbnails of nothing.

topic: the dorm room parents cannot picture before the deposit
angle: A student room is let on a plan and one bad photograph. Staging it settles an argument at a kitchen table.
palette: birch ply and slate blue with white
visualSummary: A bare dorm room up top and three staged versions in a grid below
whyNow: Late lettings run through September.
whyThisEarnsAClick: A narrow audience with a live decision, but the account just retired its Dorm badge, so leading with dorms is off message.

topic: staging a kitchen for the buyer's taste rather than the seller's
angle: The style a seller likes is not the style that sells their house. Seeing the other one side by side is the whole argument.
palette: sea salt and driftwood with pale brass
visualSummary: An empty kitchen across the top, then the same kitchen in three presets below, the least expected one sitting largest in the grid

copy.headline: Stage it for them, not you.

whyNow: Fewer and more serious autumn buyers means the buyer's taste is the one that decides.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It reframes a decision the reader assumed was theirs to make.

topic: the instruction a preset cannot take
angle: Presets cover the common case. The prompt covers the one thing about this particular room that is not common.
palette: teak and mustard over cream
visualSummary: A short typed sentence set very large on the deep blue field with a staged living room band beneath

copy.headline: Type it. Do not pick it.

whyNow: Weak.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Moderately, but this is close to the 09-05 quote card in idea if not in layout.

topic: one bathroom photograph rendered in every finish at once
angle: The room sellers skip is the room where presets differ most, because there is no sofa to carry the look.
palette: sea glass green and chalk with pale brass
visualSummary: A bare bathroom at the top and the same bathroom in several presets below in an asymmetric grid
whyNow: Complete listings win while inventory is up.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It proves the presets genuinely differ on the hardest room, but it overlaps i01 and i02 heavily.

topic: the week the buyer has the most listings to choose from
angle: A dated deadline the reader is standing in front of: the single week of the year with the most choice for buyers, which is the worst week to be an ordinary listing.
palette: caramel timber and cream with brushed steel
visualSummary: A large date phrase on the deep blue field with a claim line and a staged kitchen band below

copy.headline: 13.3% more listings than any other week.

whyNow: Realtor.com named 27 September to 3 October 2026 the best week of the year to buy, eleven days from now.
whyThisEarnsAClick: A real deadline, though the number is about buyers and the reader is a seller, so it needs a sentence of translation the frame may not have room for.
